hr_013:n1.prompt:
You are helping me evaluate Employer-of-Record (EOR) options to hire someone in a country where I have no legal entity. Before starting, ask me for any of these you don't have: the target country, the role/title, the approximate gross annual salary or budget I'm planning to offer, expected start date, and whether this is a one-off hire or part of a broader expansion plan.

Once you have those, please:
1. Research and compare at least three established EOR providers (for example Deel, Remote, Multiplier, Papaya Global, or Oyster) that support the target country, using their public pricing pages, cost calculators, or country guides.
2. For each provider, capture: their per-employee monthly fee, any setup/onboarding fee, estimated total employer cost in that country (base salary plus statutory employer contributions like social security, payroll tax, benefits, severance accrual), contract turnaround time, and notable coverage gaps or restrictions for that country.
3. Summarize what mandatory local benefits, notice periods, or termination costs apply, so total cost of employment is clear versus just gross salary.
4. Build a comparison table (provider, monthly fee, total estimated employer cost, contract speed, notable risks/limitations) so I can compare options side by side.
5. Flag anything unusual: minimum commitment periods, currency/payment constraints, or countries where a provider has known compliance issues.

Done looks like: a clear written comparison table plus a short recommendation of your top 1-2 EOR candidates with reasoning, ready for me to review.

Report back with the table, your notes on cost/compliance tradeoffs, and any open questions. Do not select a final vendor, sign up for any service, or submit any contract or agreement — prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off.

hr_013:n2.prompt:
You are helping me generate an EOR (Employer of Record) hiring quote and a locally compliant employment contract draft using {{vendor}}. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) the candidate's country, (2) their role/title, (3) proposed salary and currency, (4) start date, (5) employment type (full-time/part-time), and (6) any benefits or bonus terms I want included. Also confirm which {{vendor}} account/workspace to use — use my configured credentials to access it.

Actions to take:
1. Use {{vendor}}'s cost comparison capability (the calculateEorVersusEntityHiringCosts function) to generate a quote comparing EOR employment cost versus setting up a local entity for this hire, including employer costs, statutory contributions, and {{vendor}}'s service fee.
2. Using the candidate and role details I provide, create the employment contract draft via {{vendor}}'s contract creation endpoint (create a contract, POST /rest/contracts), ensuring it reflects local labor law requirements (probation period, notice period, statutory benefits, termination terms) for that country.
3. Confirm the contract draft and quote are both generated and linked to the same candidate/role record in {{vendor}}.

Done looks like: you have (a) a cost quote showing EOR vs. entity hiring costs for this country and role, and (b) a draft compliant employment contract ready for my review inside {{vendor}}.

Do not send the contract to the candidate or submit/finalize it — leave it in draft status pending my review. Report back with: the total estimated monthly/annual employer cost from the quote, a summary of key contract terms (salary, benefits, notice period, probation), and a direct link or reference to the draft in {{vendor}} so I can review it before it goes out.

hr_013:n3.prompt:
You are helping me track the step where a candidate signs their employment agreement through our Employer of Record (EOR) provider's onboarding platform, as part of hiring someone abroad via an EOR.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already known: the candidate's name and email, the country of hire, which EOR provider we're using, and the internal contact (likely me or our HR lead) who has access to that EOR's dashboard.

Your job in this step is preparatory and monitoring only — the actual signing must be done by the candidate themselves inside the EOR's own onboarding flow. That action is outside our control and remains a human step.

Please do the following:
1. Draft a short status-check note or checklist I can use to verify progress: confirm the candidate has received their onboarding invite from the EOR, confirm the contract was generated correctly (name, role, start date, compensation, country-specific terms), and note any deadline for signature.
2. If I have dashboard access credentials configured, check the EOR platform's candidate/onboarding status page for this hire and report back the current status (e.g., invited, in progress, signed, or overdue).
3. If no status is visible or you cannot access the platform, prepare a polling plan: how often to check back (e.g., every 1-2 business days) and a draft follow-up message I can send to the candidate or the EOR's support team nudging them if the signature is overdue.
4. Flag any blockers you notice (missing contract details, expired invite links, mismatched candidate info) so I can resolve them.

Do not attempt to sign, approve, or submit anything on the candidate's or company's behalf — this step remains a human step for the candidate.

Report back with: current signature status, the draft check-in message and polling schedule, and any blockers found.

hr_013:n4.prompt:
You are helping me initiate and track right-to-work and background checks for a new international hire being employed through our {{vendor}} employer-of-record (EOR) platform. If you don't already have them, ask me for: the new hire's full legal name, country of employment, role/title, and any details {{vendor}} requires to initiate onboarding (e.g. document upload links or ID verification steps). 

Actions to take:
1. Log into {{vendor}} using my configured credentials.
2. Locate the onboarding record for this new hire and confirm whether right-to-work verification and background check requests have been submitted; if not yet submitted, prepare and submit them using the details I provide.
3. Enable or confirm proactive compliance alerts in {{vendor}} so I'm notified of any new obligations tied to this hire's location (e.g. changes in local labor law, required documents, or deadlines).
4. Note the expected turnaround time {{vendor}} provides for these checks, and set a reminder for yourself to poll the {{vendor}} dashboard or notifications on that cadence to check status.
5. Do NOT attempt to complete, approve, or sign off on the checks yourself — the verification and background check results are generated by {{vendor}}'s own third-party pipeline on its own timeline. This remains a human step for me to review once results land, and you should not treat any interim status as final.

When you check status, report back to me: (a) confirmation the request was submitted (with date), (b) current status (pending/in review/complete/flagged), (c) any documents or actions {{vendor}} says are still needed from me or the hire, and (d) any compliance alerts that have surfaced. If results have fully landed and show "clear," flag that to me explicitly so I know the contract and payroll setup can proceed. If anything is flagged or requires escalation, summarize it clearly and stop there for my review.

hr_013:n5.prompt:
You are helping me complete country payroll, benefits, and equipment setup for a new hire we're employing abroad through {{vendor}}, our employer-of-record (EOR) platform. This follows contract signing and background checks; now we need to activate the operational side of employment.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already provided: the employee's name and country, their start date, our {{vendor}} login (use your configured credentials), which health insurance plan tier we want to offer (if choices exist for that country), whether we want to enable a retirement/401(k)-equivalent plan and at what employer contribution rate, and any equipment we need shipped (laptop, monitor, etc.) plus the delivery address.

Then, in the {{vendor}} portal:
1. Navigate to the employee's profile and locate the payroll setup section; confirm salary, pay frequency, and currency match the signed contract.
2. In the benefits section, enroll the employee in the health insurance plan I specified, confirming deductions will sync automatically with payroll.
3. If a retirement plan is available and I've asked for one, enable it and set the contribution percentage so it syncs with each payroll run.
4. If equipment provisioning is offered through the platform, submit a request using the address I provide.
5. Review all entries for accuracy before finalizing.

Done looks like: payroll is active for this employee, health insurance enrollment is confirmed and linked to payroll deductions, retirement plan (if requested) is configured and syncing, and equipment has been ordered (or you've noted it must be handled separately if unsupported for that country).

Since final activation may involve confirming benefit elections or contribution terms, prepare all selections and a summary of what will be submitted, but stop for human sign-off before finalizing enrollment. Report back with a summary of what was configured, any options you need me to choose between, and anything blocked.

hr_013:n6.prompt:
You are helping me provision workspace and system access for a new hire who is being employed abroad through an Employer of Record (EOR). This step happens after the EOR contract is signed, so this task is purely about setting up our internal systems, not the employment itself.

Before starting, ask me for any of the following if not already known: the new hire's full name, personal email (for the invite) or already-issued work email, their start date, their role/department, and which internal systems/tools beyond Google Workspace they need access to (e.g., Slack, GitHub, HR/payroll dashboard, project management tools).

Then do the following:
1. Using my configured Google Workspace admin credentials, create a new user account for the hire with the correct name, department, and start date, following our existing naming convention for email addresses.
2. Assign the new user to the appropriate organizational unit and groups based on their role/department, mirroring how similar existing employees are configured.
3. Set up appropriate group memberships and shared drive access relevant to their team.
4. If I've specified other tools needing access, prepare an itemized checklist of accounts/invites to send once Google Workspace is live (do not attempt logins/API calls to tools not specified).
5. Draft a welcome email containing the new Google Workspace login, temporary password or setup link, and instructions for first login, but do not send it — prepare it for my review.

Done looks like: the Google Workspace account is created and correctly configured, group/org-unit access is set, and a checklist plus draft welcome email are ready for me to review and send.

Report back with: the new account's email address, confirmed group/org-unit assignments, the checklist of other tool access to be granted, and the draft welcome email text. Do not send any invitations or emails without my explicit approval — stop for human sign-off before dispatching anything.
